hypothesis: Request220 signals are being diluted because the same observable changes have different meanings during reacceleration, pullback onset, continuing strength, and continuing weakness. Phase-specific specialists selected only on calibration should improve transfer without changing the target or information set.
frozen: no recurrent trading-policy replay in Request221

phase_definition.reacceleration: current observed return change > 0 and previous observed return change <= 0
phase_definition.pullback_onset: current observed return change < 0 and previous observed return change >= 0
phase_definition.continuing_strength: current observed return change > 0 and previous observed return change > 0
phase_definition.continuing_weakness: current observed return change < 0 and previous observed return change < 0
phase_definition.flat_or_sparse: all remaining states or insufficient two-step causal history

specialist_training.target: same Request219 within-day rank of five-event remaining option value
specialist_training.selection_rule: Use a phase specialist only if calibration Spearman improves by at least 0.015 over the global model and phase top-20 mean option-value lift is no worse than the global model.

forbidden: changing phase definitions after seeing Request178 fresh results
changing the Request219 target or five-event horizon
using future observations to define phase
claiming a deployable HOLD/EXIT policy from the hindsight option-value target
next_if_pass: Freeze transition conditioning, replace the hindsight option upper bound with a causal fitted continuation-value recursion, then replay recurrent HOLD/EXIT decisions.
next_if_fail: Do not hand-split the state more finely. Test an event-triggered controller focused on entry, pullback onset, and reversal events instead of scoring every POSITION observation.
